QF.id: AIFM CIII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_11

question.text: A Cat III AIF must provide its investors a quarterly report on concentration, leverage, FX and other risks within:

explanation.text: The Logic: Regulation 22 mandates that Category III AIFs provide a quarterly report to investors within 60 days of quarter-end covering financial information of investee companies and the risk-management items (concentration, FX, leverage, realisation, strategy, reputation, ESG). The Trap: 10 calendar days is the SEBI-facing activity report window (different counterparty). 30 days is the CTR timeline. 90 days is a common overseas LP-report norm but not Indian AIF norm. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C / XIX-D also test the 60-day investor-report window. XIX-A applies to Cat I/II distribution. Manager's Pro-Tip: Run the investor pack on a T+45 internal target so the T+60 regulatory window always has a 15-day buffer for IC / Trustee review. Investor reports and SEBI reports draw from the same data lake but have different cut-off standards.
